cases.raw_symptoms: Patient complains of recurrent migraine headaches for the past one year, occurring two to three times per month, predominantly over the right side of the head and associated with nausea and sensitivity to bright light. Reports frequent episodes of dizziness on standing quickly and generalized weakness by late afternoon. Appetite is reduced, with occasional craving for sweets, while thirst is low. Patient experiences excessive gas and abdominal discomfort after meals, along with irregular bowel habits alternating between constipation and loose stools. Sleep is restless with frequent dreams, and patient wakes feeling unrefreshed. Mentally, patient reports increased stress, poor concentration, forgetfulness, and irritability, with symptoms aggravated by mental exertion and relieved by rest in a quiet environment.

categorised.clinical_summary: A case of right-sided migraine and digestive disturbance characterized by mental fatigue, irritability, and physical exhaustion, suggesting a tubercular miasmatic background requiring constitutional support.

cases.clinical_notes: The fundamental disturbance is a state of chronic metabolic and nervous depletion, manifesting as right-sided cephalalgia and digestive failure. The strange, rare, and peculiar feature is the specific timing of the physical exhaustion (late afternoon) coupled with the right-sided lateralization of the migraine, pointing directly to the hepatic-digestive axis of Lycopodium.
